knowledge_gaps: The proposal is plausible but not reproducible yet: TF–IDF settings, similarity filtering, recency units and decay, epsilon, gate initialization, normalization, and history truncation are unspecified.

Naively recomputing pairwise recurrence for every prefix costs O(L³) per sequence. Bounded neighbor lists introduce approximation choices, and training/inference parity needs an explicit implementation.

A sigmoid gate bounds the coefficient, but does not control the residual's size relative to SASRec features. Near-zero initialization can also slow gate learning; feature norms and branch gradients require monitoring.

Textual recurrence may amplify generic terminology, popular items, or redundant substitutes—the same failure patterns identified in feedback. The proposal does not directly establish compatibility or current need.

The evaluation lacks a fixed tuning allocation, checkpoint-selection protocol, uncertainty estimates, and controls separating textual recurrence from extra model capacity. Originality 5 and difficulty 4 are provisional without closer prior-work comparison and runtime measurements.

follow_up_queries.reason: Establish a reproducible, efficient causal implementation and assess whether the difficulty rating accounts for numerical behavior and predictor parity.
follow_up_queries.query: For SASRec augmented with a gated residual pooling item embeddings using recency and within-prefix TF–IDF cosine recurrence, how can all causal prefix weights be computed in O(L²) rather than O(L³)? Investigate incremental similarity sums, padding and repeated-item handling, truncated-history equivalence, residual norm calibration, near-zero sigmoid gate gradients, and exact training/inference parity.

follow_up_queries.reason: Check novelty and determine whether a simpler alternative could address sustained interests with less computation or fewer textual shortcuts.
follow_up_queries.query: What existing sequential recommendation methods combine long-term interest pooling, recency weighting, item-text similarity, and gated SASRec residuals? Compare their mechanisms with a training-only TF–IDF recurrence branch, including simple recency pooling and history-aware item-transition baselines, and examine evidence concerning generic-token, popularity, and redundant-substitute shortcuts.

follow_up_queries.reason: Define an evaluation that distinguishes a useful recurrence mechanism from additional capacity and repeated validation tuning.
follow_up_queries.query: How should a fixed-budget ablation study evaluate a TF–IDF recurrence residual on SASRec across four Amazon categories using 200 validation users per category and fixed 99-negative HR@10? Investigate baseline, recency-only, uniform-pooling and shuffled-text controls; paired user bootstrap uncertainty; checkpoint and hyperparameter selection bias; and history-length, text-availability and popularity stratification, without accessing test labels or changing the evaluator.
